method: EMA 200 of daily closes (TradingView's ta.ema). ABOVE / ON / BELOW: the close is more than / within / below 0.5 x ATR(14) of EMA 200.
Two Fibonacci grids: the swing of the last 200 sessions and of the last 50. Levels 0%, 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, 78.6%, 100%, measured back from the more recent extreme.
Double fib: a big-grid level and a small-grid level within 0.5% of price. Support = nearest zone below the close, resistance = nearest above. '+EMA 200' = EMA 200 sits in the zone too.
Test: the last 200 sessions (2026-01-29 to 2026-11-13). Signal on a close, order at the next open, always in a trade after the first signal.
Stocks: Rs 1 crore spread as Rs 52,356 per stock; whole shares; 0.1% per buy and per sell; SELL (short) only on F&O stocks, others go flat.
Nifty: 10 and 20 lots of 65; 0.035% per side; 15-minute, 1-hour and daily candles; positions held overnight.
Pick: the rule with the most rupees in the first 100 sessions; its last 100 sessions are the honest result. Jev then reviews all candidates.
limits: 200 sessions is less than a year: one market phase. A rule that wins here can lose in the next phase.
Daily prices are Yahoo Finance adjusted closes; fills are at the open with no slippage beyond the cost charged.
Stock shorts need F&O futures (lot sizes are far bigger than Rs 50,000); the short side here is a paper scale model.
20 Nifty lots is about Rs 3.3 crore of exposure: 3x leverage on Rs 1 crore. The worst fall shown is per this window only.
Paper research. Not SEBI-registered advice. No orders are placed by this website.
